note:
ISO 2026-W30 runs from July 20 through July 26. Ceres is about 1.6° in ecliptic longitude from Elnath in Taurus.

**Naked eye:** 🌓 First Quarter — 11:05:36 UTC. Moderate moonlight makes timing and local sky position important for faint targets. Use Sabik, Rasalgethi as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -9.4; direct motion; 35.5% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude 3.3; retrograde motion; 6.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Station Jul 23 22:57 UTC: turns direct. Venus: Naked eye; magnitude -4.2; direct motion; 61.4% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: Naked eye; magnitude 1.3; direct motion; 94.2% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.0; direct motion; 98.8% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: In solar glare; magnitude -1.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.7; direct motion; 99.7% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Station Jul 26 19:56 UTC: turns retrograde. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.7; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.4; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** Trace the charted figure of Her, then identify Alpha2 Her at its plotted position.

**Small telescope:** M10: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M62: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M19: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Bug Nebula: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M92: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M9: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

story_candidates.dek: Sabik is a star in Oph; its declination determines which latitudes can observe it.
story_candidates.body:
Its catalogue position is approximately right ascension 17h 10m and declination -15.7°. These reference coordinates describe its sky location; they are not an observing time or a current altitude.

At the almanac’s default latitude of 45° N, this star rises and sets, reaching approximately 29° altitude at upper culmination. These are geometric calculations from declination, excluding refraction and local obstructions. Darkness and the time of culmination must still be checked for the observing date and your location.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Oph constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.

Sources: Star Almanack’s stored fixed-object and expanded Bayer catalogues; accepted constellation figures and guiding-star routes. Visibility limits are original geometric calculations from catalogue declination, not weekly predictions.
